titolo: Elon Musk: 'I'm Not MAGA' After a $400M+ Midterm Loss
angolo: From 'dark MAGA' to 'quite moderate': Musk's DealBook confession, set against a $1B Skydance bet and a SpaceX permit that arrived the same week.
descrizione: Elon Musk: 'I'm Not MAGA' After a $400M+ Midterm Loss. At the NYT DealBook Summit, speaking by video from China, Musk said he feels 'pretty foolish' about his midterm spending. The same day, Skydance CEO David Ellison confirmed Musk is a shareholder, and Texas regulators were reported to have cleared a SpaceX data center permit. We separate what is confirmed from what is only reported.

scene.testo: A man who once wore MAGA hats just said: I'm not MAGA.
He did it live, by video, from China.
And then he said he felt pretty foolish.

citazione.testo: I feel pretty foolish about having spent so much money and not seeing much for it.

scene.testo: Elon Musk spent nearly half a billion dollars on the midterms, according to NBC. Why is he backing away now?
Stay with me. There are two more stories today: Ellison's confirmation that Musk has a stake in Skydance, reportedly about a billion dollars, and a Texas air permit for SpaceX.
First, the stage. The New York Times DealBook Summit.
Host Andrew Ross Sorkin pressed him on his politics.
Musk joined from China, where he is part of President Trump's delegation to the APEC summit.
Sorkin raised his past statements on immigration and what he called MAGA stuff.
Musk's answer was blunt.
Then he softened it. He said he isn't sure what MAGA means.
If it means blind adherence to Republican policies, he says, he doesn't have that.
He called himself ideologically quite moderate, with no extreme political views.
But the record shows a different picture. Here is where it began.
In fall 2024, he campaigned with Trump at Madison Square Garden.
There, CNBC notes, he described himself as dark, gothic MAGA.
He also appeared publicly in MAGA-emblazoned hats.
AP reported he spent at least 250 million dollars backing Trump in 2024.
Then he led the Trump administration's cost-cutting effort, the Department of Government Efficiency.
In May 2025, he told a forum in Doha he would spend a lot less.
He added a catch: if he saw a reason, he would do it.

citazione.testo: If I see a reason to do political spending in the future, I will do it.

scene.testo: Weeks later came a public break with Trump over a spending bill.
Then Musk said some of his posts about the president went too far.
And the money flowed again. How much? The answer depends on which count you use.
Scripps News, citing campaign finance records, says at least 474 million dollars on the 2026 midterms.
Other outlets cite 458 million, or 445 million. The totals differ by source.
The biggest target: a Senate race between Ken Paxton and James Talarico.
Some estimates of his Texas spending run past 200 million dollars, with about 200 million aimed at the Paxton–Talarico race by one account.
Reports say 158 million dollars went to a Senate GOP super PAC that passed matching sums to a group backing Paxton.
The result? Paxton lost to Talarico.
CBS reports Democrats won the House and the Senate.
Democrats also won the Texas governor's office, where Tesla and SpaceX are headquartered.
Talarico told voters in the final days that Musk wanted Texas' land, water and tax dollars, according to Newsweek.
After winning, Talarico told ABC's The View what Texans had said.
So what did Musk say his goal had been?
To preserve divided government, he said, rather than secure unified Republican control.
He said that goal failed. He wanted checks and balances.
Still, he left a door open: maybe it would have been much worse without that spending.
He also said that if he could rewind the clock, he would have spent less money.
Now the stakes for his companies. NBC reports some incoming Democrats are talking about opening investigations over his involvement in DOGE.
But politics was only part of Wednesday's story. The other part was money.
Same summit. Different stage. David Ellison, CEO of Skydance.
Variety reports Ellison confirmed Musk has invested in Skydance.
Ellison said having Musk as a shareholder is an honor and a privilege.

citazione.testo: To have his vote of confidence and to have him as a shareholder is an honor and a privilege.

scene.testo: The amount? Semafor reported in October: about one billion dollars.
Careful: Variety says Ellison did not officially confirm that amount.
Investing.com, however, wrote that Ellison said approximately one billion. Accounts differ.
Sorkin asked if this is the start of something bigger with Starlink.
Ellison said they'd be thrilled to collaborate someday, but there's nothing right now.
And here's the twist. Skydance's HBO Max plans to air a documentary critical of Musk.
It is planned for the first quarter of next year.
Ellison's answer on editorial control: we believe in independence.
He also said he wants CBS News and CNN kept separate.
That follows the 110 billion dollar merger of Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery, which closed last month.
And now the third story of the day. It involves a rocket company and gas turbines.
Politico reported Texas regulators issued SpaceX an air permit for a data center project on Monday.
The project is valued at 24 billion dollars, near Brownsville and Starbase.
The permit covers 35 natural gas turbines, about 750 megawatts, according to Politico.
The plant would not connect to the state's electrical grid, according to reports.
Reports say it allows up to 248 tons of nitrogen oxides per year.
The agency, TCEQ, had paused such permits after Governor Greg Abbott ordered it in September.
The pause awaited a report from the grid operator, ERCOT.
Politico says the pause wasn't due to end until December 10.
A TCEQ spokesperson told Politico the agency resumed its normal permit review process.
The advocacy group Public Citizen criticized the move, saying TCEQ was trying to move permits forward quickly and quietly.
The group alleges construction may have started without the permit. That is not established.
SpaceX did not respond to Politico's requests for comment.
Reports say SpaceX shares rose about one to two percent on the news.
Notice the timing. Abbott lost his bid for reelection earlier this month.
Democrat Gina Hinojosa won the governor's race, CBS News reports.
Politics changes. Permits, rockets and server racks keep going.

visivo.testo: Politics changes. Permits, rockets and server racks keep going.

scene.testo: Musk's own words at DealBook set a new tone.
He said there are positives and negatives in both parties.

citazione.testo: I think there are positives and negatives in both parties.

scene.testo: In 2023, at the same summit, he was in a fight with advertisers.
Three stories in one day: a regret, a stake, a permit.
So is this a real shift, or a reset after a hard election? He backtracked within the same answer.
The story is still moving. Subscribe, so you don't miss the next chapter.
